scope: Nationwide public-source framework for investigating criminal and cybercrime metadata at the U.S. city/local-jurisdiction level.
coverage_limit: A literal scan of every U.S. city and every underlying record is not represented by this file. It catalogs the authoritative public sources and a normalized schema that can be applied across cities. FBI coverage varies because participation and reporting completeness differ by agency and year.

criminal_data_sources.coverage: National incident-based crime reporting by participating law-enforcement agencies
Public UCR/NIBRS crime data and agency-level reporting
Uniform Crime Reporting program and related public releases
National victimization estimates; not a city-by-city police incident database

cybercrime_sources.coverage: Public annual cyber-enabled crime complaint and loss statistics; city-level completeness is not equivalent to NIBRS
Known vulnerabilities exploited in the wild; not a city crime registry
Defensive baseline metadata for organizations and critical infrastructure

recommended_analysis: crime rates using documented population denominator
important_interpretation_rules: Do not equate reported crime with all crime occurring in a city
Do not compare cities without checking reporting coverage and population denominators
Do not infer criminality of individuals from aggregate city statistics
Do not label a person a criminal based on an allegation, arrest, or incident record without appropriate legal disposition
Cyber complaints are not necessarily verified incidents or confirmed attribution
CISA vulnerability records describe vulnerabilities, not proof that a particular city was attacked
Preserve source and methodology metadata for every statistic
privacy_security_boundary: no live targeting or operational law-enforcement information
no exploit payloads or instructions for attacking systems
status: Nationwide public-data inventory and normalized city-level criminal/cyber metadata schema uploaded for lawful statistical research.
